about: Font facts for the fonts the lab cases name, read offline from the installed fonts and the web font fixtures on this Mac. rebuild/lab/font-facts.ts resolves a CSS font declaration to FontFacts per engine from this data (DESIGN.md §1.2). The library never reads it.

machine.note: CTFontCreateForString picks substitutes from the system cascade, which depends on the machine languages recorded here (research reading only).

shapers.note: ligatures.py shapes with the HarfBuzz uharfbuzz bundles; Chrome 153 pins dfdc088c (after 14.3.1) and Firefox 156 vendors 14.3.1. ctligatures.swift shapes with this OS build's Core Text.

coreTextDefaultFeatures.note: strings of ligature entries outside the lookups and chain subtables HarfBuzz turns on by default (ligatures.py `probes` with a false third flag), over every face read; coreTextOnly lists the ones Core Text ligates by default and HarfBuzz doesn't

faceColumns.cssWeight: Core Text kCTFontWeightTrait through Blink ToCSSFontWeight (font_matcher_mac.mm:846-866); ctprobe.swift
faceColumns.coreTextGlyphU2010: CTFontGetGlyphsForCharacters(U+2010); Core Text synthesizes a hyphen glyph for fonts without one (harfbuzz_face.cc:210-220); ctprobe.swift
faceColumns.cmapU2010: best cmap maps U+2010; tables.py (fontTools getBestCmap)
faceColumns.opsz: CTFontCopyVariationAxes has opsz, checked against the fvar table (fvarAxes, tables.py)
faceColumns.morx: CTFontCopyTable morx or mort non-null (what Skia gives HarfBuzz on Apple), checked against the file; ctprobe.swift, tables.py
faceColumns.gsub: CTFontCopyTable GSUB non-null, checked against the file
faceColumns.gsubArabFeatures: GSUB features under script 'arab' (default and every language system); null when there is no GSUB; tables.py
faceColumns.cmapU0628: best cmap maps U+0628 (Arabic coverage); tables.py
faceColumns.pairKerning: where HarfBuzz puts a pair adjustment in Latin text: 'first-advance' (GPOS PairPos XAdvance on the first glyph), 'split' (kern or kerx pair machine: kern >> 1 on the first glyph), null otherwise; from the kerning column of tables.py (GPOS kern scripts and PairPos value formats, kern and kerx subtable formats) and the morx and GSUB columns (build-facts.ts pairKerning)
faceColumns.substituteForU0628: the face CTFontCreateForString(face, U+0628) returns, Blink's system fallback for a character no listed font has (font_cache_mac.mm:127-150, 199-249); ctprobe.swift
faceColumns.cmapCoverage: every code point the best cmap maps (fontTools getBestCmap), as a key of sets.coverage: sorted inclusive ranges as space-separated base 36 numbers, for each range its first code point less the code point after the previous range, then its last less its first; tables.py cmapRanges
faceColumns.coreTextAdded, coreTextWithheld: the code points CTFontGetGlyphsForCharacters gives a glyph although the cmap has none, and the cmap code points it gives none; ctprobe.swift coverage (every Unicode scalar value) against cmapRanges. Added ones are synthesized by Core Text (U+2010, U+2011, U+00A0, U+2028, U+2029, U+FEFF, U+2060, TAB, LF, CR, U+A789, variation selectors, U+202F in some fonts). The builder refuses withheld ones except for the platform UI font, where Core Text withholds [ ] U+00B7, low and double quotation marks and circled digits on this Mac (first language zh-Hans), which the cascade then draws
faceColumns.geckoRequiresAat, geckoClearedRanges: what Gecko's character map reading does to an installed font (CoreTextFontList.cpp:271-335, gfxPlatformFontList.cpp:79-155, gfxFontEntry.cpp:229-240): whether it shapes the font with Core Text (morx or mort without GSUB and GPOS, or kerx, or morx or mort with a complex script in the cmap; gfxMacFont.cpp:154-160), and the complex script ranges it clears because the font has neither morx nor a GSUB script for them; build-facts.ts geckoCharacterMap from tables.py's tables, cmapRanges and gsubScripts. Web fonts keep their map (:271). The Songti, STSong and Kaiti block list (:315-335) isn't ported
faceColumns.scriptLookups: the Unicode scripts grouped by the GSUB and GPOS script records HarfBuzz selects for them (hb_ot_layout_table_select_script, hb-ot-layout.cc:561-608: the script's tags from hb_ot_all_tags_from_script, hb-ot-tag.cc:36-181, else 'DFLT', 'dflt', 'latn'). `groups` lists the scripts whose records differ from the fallback's, grouped by equal records under every language system (required feature, features with their lookups, FeatureVariations alternates); every other script shares the fallback records. A table HarfBuzz doesn't apply counts as equal for all scripts: GSUB when the font has morx or mort, GPOS when kerx is applied (hb-ot-shape.cc:59-65, :150-185); tables.py script_lookups
faceColumns.spacingInputs: per feature group, the characters that can become a glyph at which a lookup of the group starts: `ligatures` is liga and clig (morx: common ligatures 1/2 and contextual ligatures 1/18), `calt` is calt (morx 36/0; HarfBuzz's mapping, hb-aat-layout.cc:111-132). These are the default-on features the engines turn off for non-zero letter-spacing: liga and clig in all three, calt in Blink too (font_features.cc:54-86; UnrealizedCoreTextFont.cpp:258-264; gfxFont.cpp:675-700). A GSUB lookup acts at a position only when the glyph there is in a subtable's coverage, and a morx subtable only on glyphs it gives a class, so text without these characters shapes the same with the group off. `codePoints` is encoded like sets.coverage; `unmapped` counts covered glyphs the planned substitutions can make that no character gave in the contexts tried, and a group with any can't rule text out. From the lookups and chain subtables HarfBuzz's default features plan, and the glyphs HarfBuzz gives each character alone and, for Arabic script, joined (ligatures.py spacing_inputs). null when the program failed on the face
faceColumns.ligatures: a key of sets.ligatures: the character sequences the face turns into a ligature under HarfBuzz's default features, from the font's GSUB LigatureSubst entries and morx ligature subtables (ligatures.py, which documents the derivation and what `complete` and `limits` mean), with Core Text's verdict on every string HarfBuzz ligated (ctligatures.swift). Per pattern: `positions` (every string made of one alternative per position), `exact` (every such string was shaped and ligates; false: alternatives were shaped one at a time), `feature` (the GSUB feature, or morx:<type>/<selector>), `everyContext`, `acrossMark`, `harfBuzz.spacedBlink` and `spacedGecko` (still a ligature under liga, clig, calt off, font_features.cc:54-86, and under liga, clig, dlig, hlig off, gfxFont.cpp:675-700), `coreText.default`, `spacedWebKit` (liga, clig, dlig, hlig off by OpenType tag, UnrealizedCoreTextFont.cpp:258-264) and `spacedGecko` (common ligatures off, gfxCoreTextShaper.cpp:620-622): 'all', 'some' or 'none' of the pattern's shaped strings. `coreTextOnly` lists shaped strings Core Text ligates and HarfBuzz doesn't. null when a program failed on the face

realizes.blink: families in list order; a family realizes when a web font of that name is loaded or FontCache matches an installed family (font_fallback_list.cc:149-194). PrimaryFont() looks up U+0020 with should_contain_glyph false (font.h:234-237; font_fallback_list.h:141-145), so the space only selects a unicode-range segment and the primary font is the first realized font (font_fallback_list.cc:88-128). Faces: BestStyleMatchForFamilyNS with BetterChoiceCT, CSS directional weight search (FontFamilyStyleMatchingCTMigration has no status, font_matcher_mac.mm:599-700, 296-360); no-realize falls to -webkit-standard then Times (font_cache_mac.mm:375-392)
realizes.webkit: index-0 family: the first that realizes, else the standard family (FontCascadeFonts.cpp:200-218); faces through findClosestFont's FontSelectionAlgorithm (FontCacheCoreText.cpp:445-538)
realizes.gecko: the first font of the font group; faces by WeightDistance and style distance (gfxFontEntry.cpp:1512)

tiedFaces.blink: BestStyleMatchForFamilyNS walks NSFontManager availableMembersOfFontFamily in order and stops at the first exact match; a later face replaces the choice only when BetterChoiceCT says it is better (font_matcher_mac.mm:296-360). Equally good faces: the first in families.<name>.appKitMembers
tiedFaces.webkit: FontSelectionAlgorithm::indexOfBestCapabilities is the first face not eliminated (FontSelectionAlgorithm.cpp:198-201), in the order of CTFontDescriptorCreateMatchingFontDescriptors with the family name mandatory (FontCacheCoreText.cpp:445-455), which is the order of families.<name>.faces. Equally good faces: the first
tiedFaces.gecko: FindAllFontsForStyle appends every face at the smallest weight, style and width distance to the family's matched list (gfxFontEntry.cpp:1601-1640), so tied faces can all draw text: a fact is given only where they agree

systemUI.note: CTFontCreateUIFontForLanguage(kCTFontUIFontSystem): SFNS.ttf upright and SFNSItalic.ttf italic, variable fonts whose instances are the CSS weights (ctprobe.swift prints the file of five weights), so the two faces stand for every weight

blink.source: font_cache_mac.mm:289-292 (LegacySystemFontFamily), :408-411 (MatchSystemUIFont for system-ui); -apple-system is an ordinary family name that matches no installed family (font_matcher_mac.mm:599-700; probes-chrome cross X5)

webkit.source: FontCacheCoreText.cpp:570 (-webkit-system-font, -apple-system, -apple-system-font, system-ui, ui-sans-serif); BlinkMacSystemFont is an ordinary family name that matches nothing

gecko.source: CoreTextFontList.cpp:1602-1620 (-apple-system is the system font family), gfxPlatformFontList.cpp:2237 (system-ui resolves to it); BlinkMacSystemFont is an ordinary family name that matches nothing

rules.primaryFamily: the realized family as the list names it; a generic keyword stands for itself (DESIGN.md §1.2)

mapsHyphen.blink: PrimaryFont()->GlyphForCharacter(U+2010) non-zero: HarfBuzz cmap, then SkTypeface::unicharToGlyph through Core Text on Apple (computed_style.cc:1804-1820; harfbuzz_face.cc:210-231): cmapU2010 || coreTextGlyphU2010 != 0
mapsHyphen.webkit: primaryFont().glyphForCharacter(U+2010) non-zero, from CTFontGetGlyphsForCharacters on that font (StyleComputedStyle.cpp:419-435; GlyphPageCoreText.cpp:51-73): coreTextGlyphU2010 != 0
mapsHyphen.gecko: not read by the port (Canvas substitutes as the DOM does, gecko-gaps §3.6); the value is GetFirstValidFont(U+2010) on the primary font, cmapU2010 (gfxTextRun.cpp:2277-2360)

monospace.webkit: Font::determinePitch: kCTFontMonoSpaceTrait, or a non-zero kCTFontFixedAdvanceAttribute, or the full name Osaka-Mono, MS-PGothic or MonotypeCorsiva (FontCoreText.cpp:753-785; specs/webkit-gaps.md §2.1). post.isFixedPitch is recorded per face but not read; Courier has the trait with isFixedPitch 0
monospace.blink: not read (DESIGN.md §1.2); the value follows the FontFacts definition, the WebKit notion
monospace.gecko: not read (DESIGN.md §1.2); the value follows the FontFacts definition, the WebKit notion

rules.opticalSizeAxis: the primary faces have an opsz axis (DESIGN.md §1.2); Blink reads it at layout zoom != 1, Gecko for every run, WebKit not at all

joining.blink: the face drawing U+0628: the first realized font in list order whose cmap maps it, else the primary face's Core Text substitute. 'aat' when it has morx or mort (HarfBuzz applies morx for horizontal text and switches to the dumber shaper, which reads no context: hb-ot-shape.cc:60-66, 100-101; hb-aat-layout.cc:278-282); 'opentype' when it has GSUB with 'arab' init, medi and fina, where the Arabic shaper reads the buffer context (hb-ot-shaper-arabic.cc:305-360); otherwise null
joining.webkit: not read; same value as Blink
joining.gecko: not read; same value as Blink

rules.generics: a generic keyword realizes one of the engine's default families for the script of the text; the lookup takes every candidate below and gives a fact only where all realized candidates agree, else null

fonts.about: FontFacts.fonts: one entry per family of the list, in order, with `realizes` and, for a family that realizes one face (or tied faces that agree), that face's coverage, ligatures and scriptLookups as the engine sees them. A generic keyword with more than one realized candidate gives null facts. The engine's system fallback after the list isn't resolved

coverage.blink: the cmap, plus U+2010 and U+2011 where Core Text has a glyph: HarfBuzzGetGlyph asks the cmap and, on Apple, SkTypeface::unicharToGlyph for these two only (harfbuzz_face.cc:210-231): cmapCoverage plus those two where coreTextAdded has them
coverage.webkit: CTFontGetGlyphsForCharacters, which fills the glyph pages (GlyphPageCoreText.cpp:51-73): cmapCoverage plus coreTextAdded less coreTextWithheld
coverage.gecko: the cmap (gfxFontUtils::ReadCMAP) less the complex script ranges Gecko clears in an installed font that has neither morx nor a GSUB script for them (CoreTextFontList.cpp:271-313): cmapCoverage less geckoClearedRanges

ligatures.blink: HarfBuzz shapes every font: the patterns with `spaced` from harfBuzz.spacedBlink
ligatures.webkit: Core Text shapes every font: the patterns Core Text ligates ('all' or 'some' of their strings; 'some' makes the pattern inexact) with `spaced` from coreText.spacedWebKit ('all'), plus coreTextOnly
ligatures.gecko: Core Text for a face with geckoRequiresAat (gfxMacFont.cpp:154-160), with `spaced` from coreText.spacedGecko, else HarfBuzz with harfBuzz.spacedGecko

spacingInputs.blink: the ligatures and calt groups joined; null when either has unmapped glyphs
spacingInputs.webkit: the ligatures group; null when it has unmapped glyphs. Core Text reads the same GSUB features by tag and the same morx feature settings; the characters that reach a covered glyph come from HarfBuzz's shaping
spacingInputs.gecko: the ligatures group; null when it has unmapped glyphs

scriptLookups.blink: HarfBuzz: the groups of the scriptLookups column
scriptLookups.webkit: null: Core Text's script selection isn't in source
scriptLookups.gecko: HarfBuzz for a face without geckoRequiresAat, else null

blink.source: Chrome defaults for macOS, chrome/app/resources/locale_settings_mac.grd:126-276 (read at chromium-152; the 153.0.8010.48 checkout has no chrome/app/resources), registered for Mac by chrome/browser/ui/prefs/prefs_tab_helper.cc:155-191; Blink asks GenericFontFamilySettings by the font description's script (font_selector.cc:72-89), which falls back to the common script

webkit.source: WebKit Cocoa defaults, UnifiedWebPreferences.yaml:3175-3187 (FixedFontFamily Courier), 7054-7065 (SansSerifFontFamily Helvetica), 7393-7404 (SerifFontFamily Times), 8070-8082 (StandardFontFamily Times); SettingsBaseCocoa.mm:44-50 sets per-script standard families only; FontGenericFamilies.cpp:50-66 falls back to USCRIPT_COMMON

gecko.source: Firefox macOS font.name-list prefs, modules/libpref/init/all.js:2337-2529 (XP_MACOSX), for the language groups of the lab's languages: x-western, x-unicode, ar, he, ja, ko, zh-CN, zh-TW, zh-HK, th, x-devanagari, x-khmr
